name: Interpretability
strandNote: Optional on every quant track. For AI research roles and for reading what a trained model has learned.
description: Open up small trained transformers and toy models, find the circuits and features inside, and test each claim by intervening.

levels.name: The residual stream and the logit lens

requires.why: Reads the trained tiny GPT and reuses the forward pass written in gpt levels 2 and 3.
Builds on the transformer block and the residual stream from sequence level 4.
Reads query, key and value maps, causal masks and heads from sequence level 3.
A sparse autoencoder extends the autoencoder of representations level 2, which only spans principal components.
Trains the toy model and the autoencoder with the Adam optimiser from nn-train level 1.

lessonNames.l4-lens-on-the-tiny-gpt: The lens on the tiny GPT

lessonObjectives.l1-the-stream-as-a-sum: Write the final residual stream as the embedding plus every head and MLP output, and check the sum in code.
lessonObjectives.l2-the-logit-lens: Unembed the residual stream after each layer and read where the prediction forms.
lessonObjectives.l3-direct-logit-attribution: Split a logit into the direct contribution of each component, with the final layer norm's scale frozen.
lessonObjectives.l4-lens-on-the-tiny-gpt: Apply the logit lens and direct attribution to the tiny GPT and say what each layer adds.
lessonObjectives.l5-reading-attention-patterns: Read a head's attention pattern and score it against simple rules: previous token, first token, same token.
lessonObjectives.l6-previous-token-heads: Find the previous-token head in a two-layer model and explain how it uses positions.
lessonObjectives.l7-induction-heads: Find the induction head and show that it predicts the second half of a repeated sequence.
lessonObjectives.l8-how-heads-compose: Derive the induction head's key from the previous-token head's output: K-composition.
lessonObjectives.l9-more-features-than-dimensions: Explain why sparse features can share dimensions, and measure the interference they cause.
lessonObjectives.l10-the-toy-model: Build and train the ReLU toy model of superposition in NumPy, with its gradient checked.
lessonObjectives.l11-the-pentagon: Replicate the toy-models figure: how many features a 2-D model stores as sparsity rises.
lessonObjectives.l12-sparse-autoencoders: Train a sparse autoencoder that recovers the toy model's features, and read the sparsity trade-off.
lessonObjectives.l13-knocking-out-a-head: Ablate each head by zeroing or by its mean output and rank the heads by the loss they protect.
lessonObjectives.l14-activation-patching: Patch clean activations into a corrupted run and measure the share of the logit difference recovered.
lessonObjectives.l15-patching-the-tiny-gpt: Design a clean and corrupted prompt pair for the tiny GPT and patch layer by layer.
lessonObjectives.l16-reading-attribution-graphs: Read a published attribution graph and say what it shows, what it assumes and how it was tested.
